analysis.title: Novartis (NOVN.S): 3Q26 First take: Cost control continues to drive earnings momentum, guidance upgrade suggests 2% upside risk to Core
key_insights: Novartis 3Q26 net sales were $14,522mn, broadly in line with company-compiled consensus of $14,452mn (GSe $14,365mn), a 0% or $70mn beat.

Core operating income was $6,036mn vs consensus $5,582mn, an 8% or $454mn beat (GSe $5,490mn). The beat came from lower costs: COGS 2% ($73mn) below consensus, SG&A 10% ($334mn) below, R&D 4% ($129mn) below.

The cost beat came despite prior company commentary of rising cost phasing in 2H and incremental R&D investment, with no apparent one-time positives offsetting it. GS says the quality of the beat could be questioned because the guided cost phasing did not materialise.
Core operating margin was 41.6%, 294bps above consensus of 38.6% (GSe 38.2%). Core EPS was $2.46 vs consensus $2.29.

Sales beats: Cosentyx +4% ($67mn, boosted by price), Ilaris +12% ($66mn), Zolgensma +13% ($45mn, Itvisma launch), Tafinlar+Mekinist +8% ($42mn). Misses: Pluvicto -8% (-$56mn, timing of ramp-up of new indications), Kisqali -1% (-$23mn), Scemblix -2% (-$13mn).

Novartis raised FY26 Core Operating Profit guidance to in-line to grow low-single-digit CER (previously low-single-digit decline). Net sales guidance is unchanged at low-single-digit CER growth. Net financial result and core tax rate guidance are unchanged.

The guidance midpoint implies about 2% upside to consensus core operating profit and about 1% downside to consensus net sales, the latter driven by a smaller FX tailwind (+1% vs the +1-2% consensus assumed), all else equal.
Other operating income/expense was a $250mn expense vs $53mn consensus, driven by higher provision charges (including for a long-term supply agreement) and higher restructuring expenses.

Pipeline: no meaningful changes to key near-term catalysts. OAV101 IT SMA China submission was withdrawn and VHB937 in ALS missed its primary endpoint in 3Q26. Remibrutinib for myasthenia gravis was removed from Phase 3, and the RMS submission was advanced from 2027 to 2026 (with a priority review voucher).
A $1.9bn impairment was booked on del-desiran after its miss in DM1 (carrying value $5.5bn after impairment). Pelacarsen also failed in its Phase 3 HORIZON trial.

GS expects shares to only slightly outperform on the day. Novartis has already outperformed the SXDP by 4pp since the pelacarsen and del-desiran failures. GS stays Sell with a 12-month target of CHF 113 / $136 per ADR, 11.4% downside from CHF 127.48.

market_movers.rationale: GS keeps its Sell on a 12-month ADR target of $136, 11.6% below the $153.81 price. The target is a 50:50 blend of DCF (CHF 111) and 13.5x 2027E EPS (CHF 114).

sector_views.rationale: GS rates Novartis Sell relative to its European pharma coverage universe, citing valuation after the stock outperformed the sector.

earnings_insights: 3Q26 reported 10/27: net sales $14,522mn vs company-compiled consensus $14,452mn (GSe $14,365mn).
3Q26 reported 10/27: core operating income $6,036mn vs company-compiled consensus $5,582mn (GSe $5,490mn), core operating margin 41.6% vs consensus 38.6%.
3Q26 reported 10/27: core EPS (continuing operations) $2.46 vs consensus $2.29 (GSe $2.24), up 9% y/y from $2.25 in 3Q25.
FY26 guidance: net sales growth of 1-3% CER implies about $55.6-56.7bn. Core operating income growth of 0-2% CER implies about $22.1-22.6bn. FX is a +1% tailwind on both if late-October rates hold.
GS forecast (estimates): FY26E revenue $56,571.7mn, EBIT $21,848.1mn, EPS $8.85. FY27E revenue $60,520.1mn, EBIT $23,759.9mn, EPS $9.83. Quarterly EPS estimates: 4Q26E $2.27 and 1Q27E $2.21.
Core tax rate guidance c.16.5% and core net financials c.$1.7bn, both unchanged.
risk_factors: Upside risks to GS's Sell: continued positive earnings momentum, stronger-than-expected sales from key franchises, unexpected pipeline success, and capital allocation (BD and buybacks).
Quality of the earnings beat is questionable because the guided 2H cost phasing did not appear.
Pipeline setbacks (pelacarsen, del-desiran, VHB937 in ALS) and their effect on mid-to-long-term guidance.
Patent expiries at the end of the decade, Entresto loss of exclusivity effects in 4Q26, and reports of Lutathera generic entry.
vol_and_positioning: Novartis shares have outperformed the SXDP by 4pp since the pelacarsen and del-desiran failures, per GS, which is part of the reason it expects only slight outperformance on the print.

Group core operating margin came in at 41.6%, 294bps above consensus estimates of 38.6%

following the impairment of $1.9bn in the quarter (carrying value of $5.5bn post impairment)

tension_points.bull_case: Core operating profit beat consensus by 8% ($454mn) and FY26 core operating profit guidance was raised to flat-to-up low single digits CER, implying about 2% upside to consensus.
tension_points.bear_case: The beat came from costs falling well below consensus (SG&A -10%) despite company commentary of rising 2H cost phasing and R&D investment, and sales were only in line, so the quality of the beat could be questioned.
tension_points.what_invalidates: GS does not state a specific level or event; the call and conference discussion would test whether the cost phasing still arrives in 4Q26.

theme_stances.key_argument: The bottom-line beat is strong, but its quality could be questioned because expected cost phasing in 2H did not materialise.
theme_stances.evidence: the quality of the beat could be brought into question
